desc:
Large, black bushes cover this mountain pass. Their thorny branches are clad in
small and round green leaves. A few tall alders stand on the steep slopes, and
fungi thrive in their shadows rather than the thorn bushes growing everywhere
else. While the slopes to either side are very steep, rocky and treacherous, the
floor of the pass is flat and not difficult to travel upon.
name: Narrow Mountain Pass

desc:
To the south the terrain rises towards a narrow mountain pass that runs between
steep cliff walls. Large boulders and small rocks form a rough and rocky floor
covered with dark roots and thorny brambles. The occasional black oak grows on
the sheer mountain face, limbs slowly swaying in a foul breeze.
name: Narrow Mountain Pass

desc:
Short and gnarled trees grow in dense rows here. In one area the trees have been
felled, leaving only their stumps. A crossroad is revealed in this clearing,
allowing to travel in three directions. A rocky mountain path leads south,
hugging a steep escarpment, while a trampled area in the dense undergrowth to
the east and the west looks quite walkable.
name: Mountain Crossing

desc:
This overgrown ridge is littered with broken rocks and moss-covered boulders. A
few oak trees grow oddly twisted, standing in odd angles, with dark, strangely
contorted branches moving lazily as if in a constant breeze. Thick, green grass
covers the forest floor, growing everywhere except where rocks and boulders
block it.
name: Rocky Range

desc:
Every here and there, dim grey walls are interspersed with a greener hue,
ranging from subtle hints a few feet high to dark green stains near the bottom
of the cave. The walls end upwards into an inky darkness, hiding the ceiling
from sight. A few jagged and uneven edges break up otherwise smooth wall. Dark
brown streaks resembling a deep brown mud seemingly connect each edge to each
other. Some of the more jagged edges have broken off, creating a haphazard line
of pebble-sized rocks.
name: Vast Cavern

desc:
Smooth, grey rock walls line the cave, only to be interrupted by a crack in the
northern wall. The crack twists and turns in a semi-straight line from top to
bottom, as if splitting the cave in half, effectively becoming a focal point of
the large cave. A few small strands of discarded light brown moss lie scattered
on the worn cavern floor.
name: Immense Cavern

desc:
Featuring mostly even rock walls, very small rounded, irregular cones form a
distinguishing layer to both the top and the bottom of the cave. The glacous
stalactites grow longer and denser, their pointed edges reaching over two feet
long towards the middle of the cave. Its companions that litter the cave floor
are much more subdued, stalagmites adding an uneven surface in sharp contrast to
the grey walls. A thin layer of dirty water forms tiny puddles of black water on
the cavern's floor.
name: Vast Cavern

desc:
Claw marks cover the walls of this den. Thin roots poke through the roof of the
den, indicating that there is only a few feet of soil between the top of the
cave and a forest floor. A pile of leaves and twigs lies at the back of the den,
mixed with a lot of animal hair.
name: Den under the Hills

desc:
This junction of caverns opens into a small cave to the east, a large cavern to
the west, and to the north lies yet another dark opening. The cavern's moist
air, and widely spread moss covering the stones make the ground feel very
slippery. An occasional tiny breeze of fresh air seems to flush in from the
north.
name: Junction of Caverns

desc:
Grey walls of rough rock form the eastern and the western walls of this cavern.
As if uncertain if it's to be a great, vast cavern, or a narrow tunnel, in some
places the walls are no more than a dozen feets apart, while elsewhere they
separate by dozens of yards. There are bends and twists, blind corners and
shallow alcoves.
name: Dark, Winding Cavern

desc:
This niche is but a dark secluded corner of a network of caverns expanding out
of sight to the west. The roof is surprisingly high for such a small cave and
the upper reaches are hidden in shadows. The floor is strew with boulders
discoloured in shades of yellow, brown, and green by cave-living lichens.
name: Dark Cave

desc:
Rough grey rock form the walls, floor, and ceiling of this natural cavern. The
floor is worn in places, as if being trod upon countless times. A jagged opening
to the north is partly covered by bushes. A slope at the cavern's southern end,
winding this way and that in a zig-zag manner, allows for an ascent deeper into
the cave.
name: Shadowy Grotto

desc:
A forest of oak, fir and birch covers the wide floor of a valley. Hills rise to
the south, and the forest thins out there as if it was hesitant to approach
them. Bushes and shrubs take over as the forest recedes in the shadows of the
hills. A trampled animal trail can be espied worn into the crab grass in-between
bushes where a series of switchbacks allows passage into the rougher terrain.
name: Forested Valley Floor

desc:
Large and sprawling oaks cover the landscape here, their low-hanging branches
gnarled and scraping against one another. A thick layer of lichen has formed on
the treetops, creating a dense canopy that hardly allows any light to pass
through. The forest floor reflects this darkness, with dark musty fungi growing
amongst the matte black twisting roots.
name: Tangled Woodlands

desc:
Black and gnarled trees stand close together here, forming a dense forest.
Thorny shrubs grow between trees and anywhere there is the slightest opportunity
to thrive. Low hanging branches scrape the forest floor and thick, grey lichen
hang from them like veils. Black, twisting vines crawl up trunks to disappear in
the impenetrable canopy.
name: Dark Forest

desc:
The age old trees that grow here seem to bend under the weight of their own
boughs. Vine and lichen-draped branches droop, almost to the point of touching
the ground. The undergrowth has been flattened and trampled in the western part
of the forest, at the feet of steep cliffs that rise suddenly and mark the end
of the valley.
name: Lumbering Oaks

desc:
Warm, humid air fills this cavern. A vast and endless web of fungi and vines
covers the walls from floor to ceiling. A glowing mat of moss completely covers
the floor, leaving no sign of the rock beneath it. The floor slopes steeply
downward to the south, and numerous shrubs are visible outside the cavern
entrance to the east.
name: Fungal Cavern

desc:
Thorny bushes scratch against the gnarled and twisted trees here, growing up
against the bark and intertwining with the dark vines hanging down from the
trees' branches. The terrain becomes increasingly steep to the west; a foul
rivulet forms a cut down the slope and across the forest floor, running between
stained, mottled roots.
name: Overgrown Slope

desc:
Rows of tall oaks encircle a sloping vale filled with sprawling bushes. The
branches of the trees intertwine above and a canopy of broad leaves forms a
dense roof. The ground is covered in black moss and thick, knotted roots beneath
the trees, while the bushes in the deeper vale grow too dense to allow even a
glimpse of the soil beneath.
name: Twisted Canopy

desc:
The forest grows sparse in this north-western corner of a valley nestled among
the foothills of the Emyn-nu-Fuin. However, while the trees are few here,
brambles and thorn bushes grow in abundance. Dense dark green crab grass also
thrives in this region, covering the landscape in emerald swaths.
name: Brushwood Valley

desc:
Numerous stalactites hang down from the ceiling of this sloping cavern. The
walls of the cave are covered with grey fungus and water constantly drips down
from the ceiling. The slope slants down to the south where it narrows. A worn
path along the easiest route of ascent clearly shows that this passage is used
frequently.
name: Cavernous Slope

desc:
A low, narrow corridor meets the top of a set of stairs that descends deep into
the rock. The bottom of the stairs is shrouded in impenetrable gloom. The floor
of the tunnel is worn smooth, as if countless passing feet have treaded upon the
exposed bedrock. To the north, there is an underground junction where several
corridors meet.
name: Atop a Narrow Set of Stairs

desc:
Passages from the south, the east, the west, and above meet at this underground
intersection. These passages are covered with wooden slats which rest atop the
soft dirt of the floors; these tunnels would be suitable for the transport of
heavy loads. This junction is wide and tall with solid walls and a dry ceiling.
name: Underground Crossway

desc:
Bunk beds three and four storeys high line this cramped barracks in long rows
which leave only narrow paths between them. These beds are made of wood, with
rickety frames and thin slats. Several racks and pegs on both sides of the
entrance are used for storing equipment.
name: Orkish Sleeping Quarters

desc:
Many wooden shelves line the walls of this square chamber. In the middle of the
room there is a great pile of sturdy crates. A ladder with wheels stands in the
middle beside the crates. Though there are no useful items on the shelves, dust,
broken pieces, and numerous scraps indicate that this great storeroom was once
filled with supplies and equipment.
name: Crate-filled Storeroom

desc:
The smell of dung, litter, and wet fur hangs in the air of this east-west
corridor. The floor is covered in trampled dirt and dung, a striking contrast to
a smooth and well-maintained corridor that lies through an opening heading
uphill. Numerous foot and paw prints of various creatures crisscross the grimy
floor.
name: Irregular, Malodorous Corridor

desc:
Very little care was used in the burrowing of this corridor. Scattered wooden
beams seem to barely support the ceiling, and the walls are uneven and rough. A
big stack of leaves is piled against the southern wall, next to a solid wooden
trough. The air is stagnant and foul, though the hint of a breeze flows in from
the east.
name: Irregular, Malodorous Corridor

desc:
A corridor entering from the west turns to meet a wooden cage-door to the south.
The corridor seems unfinished, as if the digging was halted halfway through the
task. The walls are uneven, some parts smoothed and level and others jagged and
rough. The ceiling is unsupported, and clods of fallen dirt rest on the floor.
The door to the south has just enough space to open fully, and not an inch more.
name: Irregular, Malodorous Corridor

desc:
The walls and floor of this corridor tell a tale of crude craftsmanship, based
more on brute force than skill. A strong acrid smell fills the air. The corridor
continues to the east while simple steps carved from the bedrock ascend to
another cavern.
name: Irregular, Malodorous Corridor

desc:
This small cave is used to train and handle bats. A large cage to the south has
a filthy floor covered with guano. Bits of fur poke up from the guano, though
discerning whether just tufts of fur or buried bat corpses would require a
closer investigation. Several wires spanning the cave just beneath the ceiling
have butchered bat corpses dangling from them. On a blood-smeared table in a
corner lie several small knives and other metal instruments in a disordered
heap, but also some small jars with berries.
name: Bat Trainer's Cave

desc:
Rows of wooden spars stretch from wall to wall just below the ceiling, forming
an intersecting network. A pungent, acrid smell fills the cage, its source
evidently the piles of bat guano on the floor. There is an opening to the
outside world in the southern wall, but it is blocked by a sturdy grille made of
narrow wooden bars.
name: Spacious Cage

desc:
A shadowed ledge has been made into a cage intended for holding animals. The
southern wall is open to the outside aside from solid wooden bars, permitting
fresh mountain breezes to enter the cage. A stout wooden door blocks a passage
into the mountain wall to the north; the door is scarred with claw marks. A
stack of leaves and twigs at the eastern wall serves as bedding for the animals.
name: Wolf Cage

desc:
A number of short fences partition this massive cave. Leather muzzles and
various kinds of whips hang from hooks and pegs on the western wall. There is a
large drinking trough next to the wall under the hooks, and fresh meat is stored
in a wooden crate next to it.
name: Warg Training Ground

desc:
This is a spacious cave with shallow burrows in the wall which contain small
piles of leaves. A grille on the southern wall offers a draft of fresh air into
the cave. On the ground, there are some cracked bones that still have some
scraps of flesh on them. There are also several large logs with deep teeth
marks. Apparently, this is a holding pen for wild animals.
name: Wolf Cage

desc:
This dark tunnel comes to an abrupt end as a massive gate made of wood stands to
the north. An opening of some kind seems to lead to the east and another
downwards inside the mountain. Walls of this tunnel are rough and hard with some
marks from the tools used to gnaw into the stone.
name: Massive Wooden Gate

desc:
The walls of this room look somewhat more polished than those of the passage
immediately to the west. Wooden planks cover the floor, and there is a fireplace
in the corner which appears to be used for cooking. A crude bed made of hay and
fur sits on the floor next to the eastern wall. This room offers a clear view of
a heavy wooden gate to the west.
name: Guard Room

desc:
A dark tunnel descending from above comes to a sudden end at a massive wooden
gate bolted securely into the rock walls from both sides. This crude creation
appears quite bulky and strong despite the lack of finesse in its construction.
The tunnel narrows as it approaches the gate and when it reaches it, the tunnel
is only as high and as wide as the gate is.
name: Dark Tunnel at a Gate

desc:
A small and narrow tunnel has been delved into the mountain, falling steeply as
it descends to the south. Tool marks are visible on the walls, and the ground
has been worn smooth by heavy traffic. The ceiling has been shored up with
numerous wooden beams.
name: Dark Tunnel

desc:
Dark, gnarled oaks shift and scrape against each other. They grow closely
together in tight rows, forming a sort of passage through these overgrown
bluffs. The thorn bushes and crab grass have been trampled flat in areas; the
trees bear scars that appear to have been caused by weapons.
name: Trampled Cordon

desc:
The terrain cants at a steep angle, overgrown with thorny bushes and gnarled oak
trees. Vines dangle down from the limbs of the trees, their lower ends scraping
against the rocky ground. Thick roots snake across the ground, covered in layers
of decaying leaves.
name: Tangled Slope

desc:
A rocky overhang protrudes from a mountainside above, creating a kind of ceiling
above parts of this shelf. Moss covers the mountain face to the north; a
dark-green background that the thorny shrubs growing here press up against. An
opening to the west offers a view of a sprawling forest with a dense canopy.
name: Cramped Shelf

desc:
A dense fog covers the wet ground of this swamp, rising up through a dense
canopy of trees. The dense fog makes it difficult to traverse this soggy ground
without running headfirst into the trunk of a tree. The swamp is flat and
featureless, offering no landmarks for any creature who might lose their
bearings.
name: Misty Swamp

desc:
Dark and putrid water covers the ground, discharging acrid fumes into the air.
Dense foliage holds these fumes close to the ground so that they form a hazy
mist. These toxic fumes obscure vision, making it difficult to keep the bearings
in the swamp.
name: Misty Swamp
